page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.ce4.2xlarge is an x86_64 architecture server instance powered by an Intel Xeon 8369HB processor running at 3.2 GHz. It features 8 dedicated physical cores with 1 thread per core, providing 8 vCPUs. The instance is configured with 64.0 GB of RAM, yielding a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, relying entirely on network-attached storage and CPU-based processing. Network connectivity is defined by a baseline bandwidth of 3 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates average performance across standard compute tasks, with a Geekbench single-core score of 1248.0 and a multi-core score of 4693.0. The processor supports AVX-512 instructions, including AVX-512_VNNI and AVX-512_BF16, which assist in vector operations. However, memory performance shows notable tradeoffs. While cached small-block read bandwidth is high at 465.3 GB/sec, large-block uncached read bandwidth drops to 37.76 GB/sec, placing it in the bottom 25% of tested instances. Similarly, Passmark database operations and memory scores fall into the bottom 25%, indicating potential bottlenecks for memory-intensive database transactions.

Given its 1:8 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, the instance offers a memory-optimized profile suitable for workloads requiring significant memory capacity relative to compute power. It is appropriate for general-purpose applications, web serving, and lightweight text or image processing. However, due to weak database operation benchmarks and poor performance in medium-sized LLM inference tasks, such as 7B model text generation at 5.5 tokens/sec, it is less suited for heavy database workloads or complex machine learning inference. The dedicated CPU allocation provides stable execution for sustained workloads, offering a predictable resource density for non-storage-heavy applications.
